title: Block Optimize config apply when quality gate fails + surface failure reasons
author: Jordan Lee
description:
Context: Optimize recommendations can change serving behavior (batching / caching / quantization profiles). We already persist gate runs and compute pass/fail, but there were still paths where an operator (or automation) could call the apply endpoint even if the gate was failed or still running. This PR enforces quality gating at the final boundary: the ApplyConfig operation.

What this PR does: (1) Adds a mandatory precondition check in OptimizeService ApplyConfig: if the target route/policy requires gating, the request must reference a gate_run_id and that gate run must be in PASSED or OVERRIDDEN state at time of apply. (2) Returns explicit, structured failure reasons (reason_code + human message) and stable identifiers for the UI/automation to link to the gate artifacts. (3) Adds a Console deep-link URL and API field to allow the Console to render “Blocked by quality gate” with one click to inspect the run.

Key behavior changes: - If gate is FAILED => ApplyConfig returns HTTP 409 with code QUALITY_GATE_FAILED, includes gate_run_id, gate_status=FAILED, failing_metrics summary (top 3), and a console_url. - If gate is RUNNING/PENDING => ApplyConfig returns HTTP 409 with code QUALITY_GATE_PENDING and includes a recommended retry_after_seconds. - If gate is missing but required => ApplyConfig returns HTTP 400 with code QUALITY_GATE_REQUIRED (this is the "safe by default" behavior). - If policy does not require gating (legacy/internal routes in staging) => unchanged behavior.

Non-goals: This PR does not implement override approval flows (handled in pr-19537) and does not add per-route policy configurability (handled in pr-19588). It does include forward-compatible fields in the error response to avoid another API churn when those land.

Testing: Added unit tests for gate status transitions and ApplyConfig error mapping; added integration tests to ensure ApplyConfig blocks on FAILED and PENDING gates, and allows PASSED.

Rollout plan: This is guarded behind feature flag optimize.quality_gates.enforce_apply=true (default off). We will enable in staging first, then for internal dogfood routes, then limited beta. Flag will be flipped on alongside Console UI work.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] OpenAPI updated - [x] Error codes documented - [x] Structured log added for blocked applies (for audit + debugging)

Refs: ENG-3921 (state machine), ENG-3927 (audit log events), related PRs: pr-19523 (eval-harness wiring), pr-19537 (overrides).
commits: optimize: enforce gate precondition in ApplyConfig
api: add GateFailureInfo + error codes to OpenAPI schema
console-link: return gate_run_id + console_url on failures
tests: integration coverage for failed/pending/passed gate scenarios
conversation:
Noah Patel (review): We should be careful about the “missing gate_run_id but required” path. If someone is doing a manual apply during incident response, do we want a hard block? Also, please confirm there’s no way to bypass by using an older PASSED gate.

Jordan Lee (author): Agree on incident response, but we’re keeping bypass out of band (admin-only override flow lands in pr-19537). For now, safe-by-default means hard block if gating is required. Re older gate: this PR enforces that gate_run.config_diff_hash matches the apply request’s config diff hash (and model_family/hardware_sku when present). So you can’t “reuse” a prior PASSED gate for a different diff.

Chloe Martin (review): API response shape: the Console needs a stable code + a user-safe message. Please avoid leaking metric internals (prompt ids, raw examples) in the error payload.

Jordan Lee (author): Updated. Error payload now includes: reason_code, summary_message, gate_run_id, gate_status, failing_metrics=[{metric_name, delta, threshold}] and console_url. No prompt ids, no raw artifacts. Full details remain behind gate run artifacts.

Benji Okafor (review): Where does policy come from? I see OptimizePolicy.requiresQualityGate() defaulting to true for “Optimize-generated” diffs but false for “manual”. That seems risky.

Jordan Lee (author): Good catch. I removed the manual/optimize heuristic. Policy lookup is now route-scoped with a fallback default. In this PR fallback is conservative for production routes: requires gate unless explicitly allowlisted (staging/internal). Per-route configurability lands in pr-19588; here we use the existing policy bundle with a temporary default.

Yara Haddad (review): Can we make the 409 errors retryable? Our recommender pipeline will hammer apply if it doesn’t know it’s a transient PENDING.

Jordan Lee (author): Added retry_after_seconds on QUALITY_GATE_PENDING and set an explicit “is_retryable: true”. QUALITY_GATE_FAILED is “is_retryable: false” unless a new gate is run.

Marcus Lin (review): Please add an audit-friendly log event when apply is blocked (who attempted, route, gate_run_id, reason_code). Also ensure the event doesn’t include request payloads.

Jordan Lee (author): Added structured log optimize.apply.blocked_by_quality_gate with actor_id, account_id, route_id, gate_run_id, reason_code, and request_id only.

CI note: First integration run failed due to a test assuming 400 for pending gates; updated to 409 and added retry_after_seconds assertion. Re-run passed.

Final: Approved (Noah, Chloe, Marcus).
release_notes: Optimize: Applying a cost optimization config now enforces quality gate outcomes. Applies will be blocked if the gate is pending/failed, and the API returns explicit failure reasons plus a link to gate run results for debugging.
